title: Build a Production Search Engine: From Inverted Index to Ranking + Caching
summary: Implement a working text search engine end-to-end: inverted index + tokenizer, BM25 ranking, query parsing, caching layer, latency benchmarking. Exercises every algorithmic primitive — hashing, sorting, graphs, dynamic programming, and the production constraints that turn algorithm theory into engineering practice.
contentIntro:
## What you'll build

A working text search engine: ingest documents, build an inverted index, parse + execute queries, rank results using BM25, cache hot queries, report latency benchmarks.

Not a full Elasticsearch — a tractable system that exercises every CS-foundations concept. By the end you have a defended artifact + benchmark report demonstrating production-quality algorithm engineering.

## What you'll demonstrate

- You understand how algorithmic primitives (hashing, sorting, graph algorithms, dynamic programming) compose into real systems.
- You can design + implement a non-trivial system from spec.
- You can profile, identify bottlenecks, optimize.
- You can produce a writeup explaining design decisions, alternatives considered, and lessons learned.
contentUndergrad:
## Why this capstone

Most algorithm courses end at 'here's how Dijkstra works, here's a graph problem to solve.' Real algorithmic engineering is composing primitives into systems. Search engines are the perfect proving ground: every primitive matters (tokenization needs tries, indexing needs hashing, ranking needs sorting + heap operations, caching needs LRU, query suggestions need DP for edit distance).

By the end you have a complete codebase that's a portfolio piece + a benchmark report demonstrating production engineering thinking.

## Pacing

4 weeks at ~5-8 hrs/week. Most time: milestone 3 (ranking + caching) + milestone 4 (benchmarking + final report). Milestones 1-2 are infrastructure.

## Tools

- Python or Rust or Go — your choice. The capstone library code stays standalone.
- A small text corpus (Project Gutenberg, English Wikipedia subset, or papers from arXiv).
- Standard timing + memory profiling tools (cProfile, perf, instruments).
- Locust or wrk for load testing.

## Out of scope

- Distributed search (sharding, replication). Single-machine implementation only.
- Vector / embedding-based search. Text + BM25 only.
- Production-grade query parsing (Lucene-equivalent). Simple AND/OR/NOT only.
- Faceted search, aggregations, filters. Hit list only.
contentGrad:
## Notes for the experienced

If you've worked on production search systems, the value here is the **integrated systems view**. Most search engineers focus on one component (ranking, indexing, query parsing); this exercises all of them.

Likely places to over-engineer:

- Implementing your own SkipList for posting lists. Use a sorted vector unless you've measured that it's a bottleneck.
- Tuning BM25 parameters before measuring baseline. $k_1 = 1.2$, $b = 0.75$ are sane defaults.
- Building a complex query parser. The capstone wants AND/OR/NOT only.

The rubric specifically rewards: clean composition of primitives, honest benchmarking, intelligent optimization choices.

## Variants

- **Vector-search variant**: replace BM25 with embedding-based retrieval (sentence-transformers + FAISS). Different algorithmic primitives; same overall engineering.
- **Code-search variant**: index source code (with AST-aware tokenization). More complex tokenizer; same indexing structure.
- **Distributed variant**: shard the index across multiple processes; aggregate results. Adds network + consistency considerations.

milestones.title: Tokenizer + inverted index
milestones.description:
Build a basic tokenizer (lowercase, strip punctuation, split on whitespace, optional stemming via Porter algorithm). Build the inverted index: for each token, store a posting list of (document ID, term frequency).

Ingest a small corpus (~10,000 documents). Measure index size, build time, query latency for AND/OR queries.

**Deliverables**: code (tokenizer + indexer + simple query handler) + a `tokenizer.md` writeup justifying tokenization choices + benchmark report.

milestones.title: BM25 ranking + query expansion
milestones.description:
Implement BM25 ranking. Re-test queries from milestone 1 + add new queries with multiple terms. Compare ranked results vs unranked (boolean) results.

Optional bonus: implement edit-distance-based query expansion (Levenshtein DP) for typo tolerance — if 'transfomer' returns 0 results, try 'transformer' as a candidate.

**Deliverables**: BM25 implementation + a `ranking.md` writeup + comparison report (boolean vs BM25-ranked) + at least 10 example queries with their results.

milestones.title: LRU cache + scaling
milestones.description:
Add an LRU cache for hot queries. Pick a cache eviction policy (LRU, LFU, ARC) + justify. Measure cache hit rate on a realistic query workload.

Measure latency improvements vs uncached. Stress-test with concurrent queries. Identify bottlenecks via profiling. Optimize one bottleneck (e.g., switch from sorted arrays to skip lists for posting list intersection).

**Deliverables**: cache implementation + a `caching.md` writeup + cache hit rate analysis + before/after latency comparison + a documented optimization with measured impact.

milestones.title: Final benchmark + design defense
milestones.description:
Run a comprehensive benchmark: query latency under varied load (1, 10, 100, 1000 concurrent queries), with realistic query mix (popular queries hit cache, long-tail queries miss). Compare against a baseline (Whoosh, Tantivy, or your own naive implementation).

Write a final report defending the design: what algorithmic primitives you chose + why, what alternatives you considered, what failures you encountered + how you fixed them.

**Deliverables**: comprehensive benchmark report + design-defense writeup (~1500 words) + a video or screen recording demoing the working search engine.
